results.question: Find the average travel time (in days) for vessels traveling between the Port of Valparaiso and the Port of Singapore in the first half of 2021, ranked by the average travel time in ascending order.
results.gold_sql: SELECT route, AVG(travel_time) as avg_travel_time FROM VesselTravel WHERE route = 7 AND departure_date >= '2021-01-01' AND departure_date < '2021-07-01' GROUP BY route ORDER BY avg_travel_time ASC;
results.baseline_sql:
SELECT AVG(v.travel_time) AS avg_travel_time
FROM VesselTravel v
INNER JOIN Routes r ON v.route = r.route_id
WHERE r.departure_port = 'Valparaiso'
  AND r.arrival_port = 'Singapore'
  AND v.departure_date >= '2021-01-01'
  AND v.departure_date < '2021-07-01'
ORDER BY avg_travel_time ASC;
results.pipeline_sql:
SELECT AVG(vt.travel_time) AS avg_travel_time
FROM VesselTravel vt
JOIN Routes r ON vt.route = r.route_id
WHERE r.departure_port = 'Valparaiso'
  AND r.arrival_port = 'Singapore'
  AND vt.departure_date >= '2021-01-01'
  AND vt.departure_date < '2021-07-01'
GROUP BY r.route_id
ORDER BY avg_travel_time ASC;

results.question: What are the total copper exports and CO2 emissions from Chile between 2016 and 2018?

results.question: List the intelligence operations and their corresponding threat levels, and rank them based on their threat level and budget.

CASE 
  WHEN threat = 'High' THEN 1
  WHEN threat = 'Medium' THEN 2
  WHEN threat = 'Low' THEN 3
END AS threat_rank
FROM intel_ops_threat
ORDER BY threat_rank, budget DESC;
results.pipeline_sql:

       CASE WHEN threat = 'High' THEN 3
            WHEN threat = 'Medium' THEN 2
            ELSE 1 END AS threat_rank,
       ROW_NUMBER() OVER (ORDER BY CASE WHEN threat = 'High' THEN 3
            WHEN threat = 'Medium' THEN 2
            ELSE 1 END DESC, budget DESC) AS overall_rank
FROM intel_ops_threat;

results.question: Determine the percentage of sales for each product category in each state

results.question: Who has the highest number of wins as a coach for each team in a season?
results.gold_sql: SELECT c.TeamID, c.CoachName, COUNT(CASE WHEN h.HomeTeamResult = 'Win' THEN 1 END) + COUNT(CASE WHEN a.HomeTeamResult = 'Win' THEN 1 END) AS Wins FROM Coach c LEFT JOIN Match h ON c.TeamID = h.HomeTeamID AND h.HomeTeamResult = 'Win' LEFT JOIN Match a ON c.TeamID = a.AwayTeamID AND a.HomeTeamResult = 'Win' GROUP BY c.TeamID, c.CoachName ORDER BY Wins DESC;
results.baseline_sql:
SELECT T1.TeamID, T2.CoachID, T2.CoachName, COUNT(*) AS WinCount
FROM Coach T1
JOIN Match T2 ON T1.TeamID = T2.HomeTeamID
WHERE T2.HomeTeamResult = 'Win'
GROUP BY T1.TeamID, T2.CoachID, T2.CoachName
ORDER BY T1.TeamID, WinCount DESC;
results.pipeline_sql: SELECT CoachName, COUNT(*) AS total_wins FROM Coach JOIN Match ON Coach.TeamID = Match.HomeTeamID AND Match.HomeTeamResult = 'Win' GROUP BY Coach.TeamID, CoachName ORDER BY Coach.TeamID, total_wins DESC;

results.question: Which team has the highest number of wins in the 'basketball_games' table?
results.gold_sql: SELECT name AS team, MAX(home_team_wins + away_team_wins) AS highest_wins FROM (SELECT name, CASE WHEN home_team = team_id AND home_team_score > away_team_score THEN 1 ELSE 0 END + CASE WHEN away_team = team_id AND away_team_score > home_team_score THEN 1 ELSE 0 END AS home_team_wins, CASE WHEN home_team = team_id AND home_team_score < away_team_score THEN 1 ELSE 0 END + CASE WHEN away_team = team_id AND away_team_score < home_team_score THEN 1 ELSE 0 END AS away_team_wins FROM basketball_teams JOIN basketball_games ON basketball_teams.team_id = basketball_games.home_team OR basketball_teams.team_id = basketball_games.away_team) AS subquery GROUP BY name;
results.baseline_sql:
SELECT bt.name, COUNT(*) AS wins
FROM basketball_games bg
JOIN basketball_teams bt ON bg.home_team = bt.team_id
WHERE bg.home_team_score > bg.away_team_score
GROUP BY bt.name
ORDER BY wins DESC
LIMIT 1;
results.pipeline_sql: SELECT basketball_teams.name, COUNT(basketball_games.game_id) as total_wins FROM basketball_teams INNER JOIN basketball_games ON basketball_teams.team_id = basketball_games.home_team AND basketball_games.home_team_score > basketball_games.away_team_score GROUP BY basketball_teams.team_id ORDER BY total_wins DESC LIMIT 1;

INNER JOIN investments i ON c.client_id = i.client_id
GROUP BY c.client_id

results.question: What is the difference in the average duration of closed cases between attorneys in the "criminal_defense" department, ordered by the difference?
results.gold_sql: SELECT attorney_id, AVG(duration) - LAG(AVG(duration)) OVER (PARTITION BY attorney_id ORDER BY attorney_id) as difference FROM cases WHERE status = 'closed' GROUP BY attorney_id ORDER BY difference;

results.question: Calculate the year-over-year revenue growth for each restaurant.
results.gold_sql: SELECT restaurant_name, (revenue - LAG(revenue) OVER (PARTITION BY restaurant_name ORDER BY year)) / ABS(LAG(revenue) OVER (PARTITION BY restaurant_name ORDER BY year)) as revenue_growth FROM restaurants;
results.baseline_sql: SELECT restaurant_id, restaurant_name, year, revenue, LAG(revenue, 1, 0) OVER (PARTITION BY restaurant_id ORDER BY year) AS prev_year_revenue, CASE WHEN LAG(revenue, 1, 0) OVER (PARTITION BY restaurant_id ORDER BY year) = 0 THEN NULL ELSE ((revenue - LAG(revenue, 1, 0) OVER (PARTITION BY restaurant_id ORDER BY year)) / LAG(revenue, 1, 0) OVER (PARTITION BY restaurant_id ORDER BY year)) * 100 END AS yoy_growth FROM restaurants;
results.pipeline_sql:
SELECT restaurant_name, year, revenue,
    ((revenue - LAG(revenue, 1, NULL) OVER (PARTITION BY restaurant_name ORDER BY year)) * 100.0 / NULLIF(LAG(revenue, 1, NULL) OVER (PARTITION BY restaurant_name ORDER BY year), 0)) as growth_rate
FROM restaurants
GROUP BY restaurant_name, year
ORDER BY restaurant_name, year;

results.question: What is the total duration of workout sessions for users who have completed at least 5 sessions of a specific workout type (e.g. cycling)?
results.gold_sql: SELECT SUM(duration) FROM workout_sessions_details WHERE workout_type = 'Cycling' AND user_id IN (SELECT user_id FROM workout_sessions_details GROUP BY user_id HAVING COUNT(*) >= 5);
results.baseline_sql:
WITH workout_counts AS (
    SELECT 
        user_id,
        workout_type,
        COUNT(*) AS session_count
    FROM 
        workout_sessions_details
    GROUP BY 
        user_id, workout_type
    HAVING 
        COUNT(*) >= 5
)
SELECT 
    SUM(d.duration) AS total_duration
FROM 
    workout_sessions_details d
JOIN 
    workout_counts wc ON d.user_id = wc.user_id AND d.workout_type = wc.workout_type;
results.pipeline_sql: SELECT user_id, workout_type, SUM(duration) AS total_duration FROM workout_sessions_details WHERE user_id IN (SELECT user_id FROM workout_sessions_details GROUP BY user_id, workout_type HAVING COUNT(*) >= 1) GROUP BY user_id, workout_type ORDER BY total_duration DESC;

results.question: What is the maximum consecutive number of days with a financial wellbeing score below 60 for each customer?
results.gold_sql: SELECT customer_id, MAX(consecutive_below_60) FROM (SELECT customer_id, score_date, financial_wellbeing_score, COUNT(*) FILTER (WHERE financial_wellbeing_score < 60) OVER (PARTITION BY customer_id ORDER BY score_date ROWS BETWEEN UNBOUNDED PRECEDING AND 1 PRECEDING) AS consecutive_below_60 FROM customer_scores) subquery GROUP BY customer_id;
results.baseline_sql:
SELECT customer_id,
       MAX(day_diff) AS max_consecutive_days_below_60
FROM (
    SELECT customer_id,
           score_date,
           financial_wellbeing_score,
           ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY customer_id ORDER BY score_date) AS row_num,
           ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY customer_id ORDER BY score_date DESC) - 
            ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY customer_id ORDER BY CASE WHEN financial_wellbeing_score < 60 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS grp
    FROM customer_scores
    WHERE financial_wellbeing_score < 60
) AS grouped
GROUP BY customer_id, grp
JOIN (
    SELECT customer_id, MAX(day_diff) AS day_diff
    FROM (
        SELECT customer_id, score_date, financial_wellbeing_score,
               ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY customer_id ORDER BY score_date) AS row_num,
               ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY customer_id ORDER BY score_date DESC) - 
                ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY customer_id ORDER BY CASE WHEN financial_wellbeing_score < 60 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS grp
        FROM customer_scores
        WHERE financial_wellbeing_score < 60
    ) sub
    GROUP BY customer_id, grp
) sub2 ON grouped.customer_id = sub2.customer_id AND grouped.grp = sub2.grp;
results.pipeline_sql:
SELECT customer_id, COUNT(*) AS max_consecutive_days
FROM customer_scores
WHERE financial_wellbeing_score < 60
GROUP BY customer_id;
